A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MobileRL framework, model backbones, and core experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original AndroidWorld and AndroidLab results, component ablations, trajectory analyses, and reward-model evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds AndroidControl results and an image-resolution comparison, alongside revised MobileRL-9B results.

M1.justification: The three-stage framework and SPA, AdaPR, and FCF components remain. However, v2 adds Home and Wait actions to the action space and changes the stated reasoning-refinement scoring criterion from conciseness and log-probability to correctness. Negative-trajectory pruning remains, relocated to Appendix B.3.

E1.justification: v2 adds AndroidControl to SFT training and evaluates its Low and High settings on 8,444 test samples. This extends evaluation from interactive task completion to static action prediction using step instructions or overall goals and interaction history. AndroidWorld and AndroidLab coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same interactive comparators. The new AndroidControl comparison in Table 2 evaluates 7B and 72B UI-Tars and UI-Genie variants, including the previously unevaluated UI-Genie-7B, providing a limited extension of the comparator set.

E3.justification: Reported SFT corpus sizes change from 500k and approximately 71.4k steps to 97.9k and 23.6k. v2 replaces compressed-image experiments with full-resolution results and raises the maximum pixel setting from 500,000 to 5,000,000. The fixed 4:1 RL mixture becomes backbone-dependent training, with AndroidWorld-only RL selected for 9B. AndroidControl also introduces distinct Low/High evaluation procedures and action-matching rules.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds image-resolution sensitivity across training stages, Appendix D.1 reports backbone-dependent effects of mixed training, and Table 2 compares offline performance before and after RL. Existing component, complexity, step-efficiency, pruning, and case-study analyses remain; the pruning analysis is moved to the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run ablation averages, eight trials for the complexity-based pass@k analysis, and training curves with 95% confidence intervals. No changed run counts, seed reporting, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are specified.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces MobileRL-9B's 75.8/46.8 success rates with 80.2/53.6 under revised settings; Table 6 retains the earlier values as compressed-image results. The 7B scores remain 72.0/42.5. New AndroidControl results include 9B Low/High success rates of 95.9/77.5 before RL and 94.3/73.9 after RL. Figure 1 also adds train/test learning curves.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 revises the GRPO formulation from state-conditioned action groups to complete trajectories sharing an initial state and instruction, with a trajectory-level advantage. v1's separate time-averaged SPA advantage equation is removed. The SPA reward expression is algebraically equivalent, and neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The framework, algorithm, and state-of-the-art claims remain, with revised headline results. v2 removes the claim that MobileRL is deployed in AutoGLM products. It also changes the claimed 7B AndroidWorld margin from +7.8% to +16%, although Table 1 still shows 72.0 versus 64.2, a 7.8-point difference.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's brief future-work discussion and reward-model caveat, Appendix E explicitly identifies absent out-of-domain public-app evaluation, incomplete XML coverage, reward-model bias, and substantial rollout resource constraints. Appendix B.3 adds explanations for resolution sensitivity. The limitations also connect reward-model problems to selecting AndroidWorld-only RL for the strongest 9B model.

D1.justification: v2 adds SFT learning-rate schedules, Llama-Factory packing details, dataset composition and construction, sanitization procedures, AndroidControl input/action conversions, and hardware/runtime information. The implementation is described as Verl-based instead of AgentRL-based. Existing XML preprocessing and reward-model instructions are retained through relocation; the stated code-access URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects AdaPR to experience replay and FCF to curriculum learning, adding Mnih, Zha, Matiisen, and Narvekar citations. It also adds A3 and UI-Agile references and replaces the AgentRL implementation citation with HybridFlow/Verl. The broader mobile-agent research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the narrative remain. Edits add contribution bullets, rewrite the problem and GRPO exposition, shorten the conclusion, and reorganize supporting material: pruning moves to Appendix B.3, XML preprocessing becomes Appendix C, and reward-model material is nested within the expanded data-collection appendix.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains a train/test panel, and new tables present AndroidControl results, resolution comparisons, data composition, and action mappings. Complexity plots are rearranged with common vertical scales, and case-study composites are substantially enlarged and reformatted. Existing pruning and reward curves are relocated. The reasoning-free SFT plot is also relabeled as Table 3.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves reproducibility and assessment of applicability through detailed data/evaluation documentation, the resolution comparison explaining revised scores, and concrete limitations. AndroidControl results also reveal an offline performance tradeoff after RL. These gains address important documentation and validation gaps in v1. The erroneous +16% 7B claim, understated offline declines, and some cross-reference problems temper but do not outweigh the improvement.
